bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM says Constitution strengthens democratic traditions, inspires national unity
bihar_raw_news.content: Governance 1 min Read Bihar CM says Constitution strengthens democratic traditions, inspires national unity "Our Constitution, based on the fundamental ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, is not merely the foundation of the country's system of governance, but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity," Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said. PTI Published On Nov 26, 2026 at 11:32 PM IST Set ETGovernment as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday urged people to uphold the core values of the Constitution , including justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, saying it is not merely the foundation of the country's governance system but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity. On the occasion of Constitution Day , he led a padayatra covering around 2 km in Bettiah town of West Champaran district - from Sagar Pokhra to Raj Deorhi. NDA workers and supporters from surrounding assembly constituencies also took part in the procession. Choudhary addressed party workers at Raj Deorhi, highlighting the importance of constitutional values, democratic institutions and national unity . Earlier in the day, in a post on X on the occasion of Constitution Day, he said the Constitution strengthens India's democratic traditions and inspires the nation to preserve its unity and integrity. "Our Constitution, based on the fundamental ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, is not merely the foundation of the country's system of governance, but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity," the CM said. "It inspires us to uphold the country's unity and integrity while strengthening our democratic traditions. On the occasion of Constitution Day, let us all resolve to embrace the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution in our lives, remain committed to democratic values, and further strengthen the spirit of fraternity and national unity," he added. India observes Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Diwas , every year on November 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) , chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL), Tamil Nadu , on 25 November 2026. Key Points: Project Overview: The project involves developing a 900-metre-long second container terminal at Kamarajar Port. Annual container-handling capacity: 2 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs) . It will be developed in two phases: Phase I: Capacity of 1.1 million TEUs. Phase II: Capacity of 0.9 million TEUs. Press Information Bureau Implementation Model – DBFOT: The project will follow the Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) model. The private concessionaire will design, construct, finance and operate the terminal. The concession period will be 40 years , including a construction period of 48 months. Capacity to Handle Large Container Vessels: The new terminal is designed to accommodate large mainline container ships. It will be capable of handling vessels of up to 24,346 TEUs and 400 metres in length. The 18-metre design draft will enable larger vessels to access the terminal. Existing Performance of Kamarajar Port: Handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY 2025–26. Container traffic exceeded 7 lakh TEUs during the same period. Existing container terminal capacity: 0.8 million TEUs annually. Actual container handling: approximately 0.7 million TEUs, representing around 88% capacity utilisation . Container traffic at Kamarajar Port grew at approximately 9.9% CAGR over the preceding five years, compared with around 7% growth nationally. Alignment with National Maritime Initiatives: Maritime India Vision 2030: Aims to enhance port infrastructure, maritime trade and logistics efficiency. Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047: Provides a long-term framework for developing India's maritime sector. Atmanirbhar Bharat: The project will strengthen domestic port capacity and reduce dependence on foreign transshipment infrastructure. About Kamarajar Port Limited: Formerly known as Ennore Port Limited . Located on the eastern coast of Tamil Nadu, near the Chennai industrial region. It is wholly owned by Chennai Port Authority under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. It handles coal, petroleum products, LNG, LPG, containers, automobiles and general cargo. During FY 2025–26, it recorded revenue of approximately ₹1,280 crore and profit before tax of ₹924 crore. bihar_raw_news.title: Delhi- Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Delhi-Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes Breaking News Delhi-Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes By Ananya Sharma November 27, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Delhi and Bihar are set to introduce year-round interstate bus services on 18 routes, with around 200 AC and non-AC buses connecting the national capital with destinations across Bihar, Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Singh said on Thursday. The services are expected to benefit nearly 20 lakh people from Bihar and Purvanchal who live and work in Delhi, as well as other passengers travelling between the two states. The proposed network is being introduced under a reciprocal transport agreement between Delhi and Bihar. Officials said the services are likely to be inaugurated on Friday, although operating timings have not yet been finalised. Fares are expected to be around Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000 for sleeper and non-sleeper categories. The routes will connect Delhi with destinations including Araria, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Darbhanga, East Champaran, Gaya, Kishanganj, Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Nawada, Patna and Purnia. The report also refers to destinations in the Bhagalpur region. Singh said the agreement would provide more convenient and accessible travel, particularly during peak seasons when passengers face heavy rush and limited train-ticket availability. The services are also intended to ease overcrowding on existing bus connections during festivals and other periods of high demand. To expand interstate transport capacity, the Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses for interstate operations, officials said. A further 150 buses are expected to be deployed through the public-private partnership model. Officials described the planned services as an environment-friendly public-transport initiative that would strengthen connectivity between Delhi and Bihar. The final schedule, route-wise frequency and operational arrangements had not been announced in the report. national_raw_news.title: 45th India International Trade Fair to conclude in New Delhi today
national_raw_news.content: The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will conclude today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Organised annually by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, it is one of India’s leading multi-product trade exhibitions. The theme of the fair this year is Vikas aur Virasat. An Award Presentation Ceremony was held yesterday, recognising outstanding displays and presentations by participating states and exhibitors. In the States and Union Territories category, Tamil Nadu was honoured with the gold award, Kerala received the silver award, Madhya Pradesh bagged the bronze award, while Tripura received the commendation prize. In the Ministries and Government Departments category, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) received the Gold Medal, the Ministry of Railways received the Silver Medal, and the Ministry of Textiles received the Bronze Medal. During the awards ceremony, Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh were recognised as partner states, while Assam, Delhi, Jharkhand and West Bengal were acknowledged as focus states for IITF 2026. Talking to the media, ITPO Chairman Jawed Ashraf said that this year the fair witnessed a significant increase in footfall compared to last year. He also highlighted that exhibitors witnessed higher business this year compared to the previous edition.

national_raw_news.title: India presents vision and roadmap for hosting 2036 Olympics before IOC Future Host Commission
national_raw_news.content: India presented its “vision and proposed roadmap” for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games in an online interaction with the International Olympic Committee’s Future Host Commission yesterday. The 30-minute presentation was followed by a brief discussion with the Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic-led nine-member Future Host Commission. The presentation covered proposed host city Ahmedabad’s preparedness, including sports infrastructure and the support extended by the city, state, and central authorities to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). It also covered India’s experience in hosting major international sporting events, proposed venue development plans, and the long-term vision for delivering the Games. Germany, Hungary, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, South Africa and Türkiye are the other countries that are bidding for the 2036 Games. After the presentation, the IOC will conduct an “anonymous survey” to get a sense of the general public’s view on India’s bid. The survey is expected to be done in the third week of December and will have a bearing on the evaluation of India’s bid in March next year, following which the phase of Strategic Dialogue will start. During this phase, the interested countries will be expected to provide an initial response to the Future Host Questionnaire and core financial guarantees.

national_raw_news.content: The Lok Sabha has been reconvened from Monday, while the Rajya Sabha will resume its sitting from Wednesday to transact essential government business. The sittings of both the Houses, subject to exigencies of the Business, may conclude on the 3rd of December. There would be no Question Hour, Zero Hour, or Private Members’ Business during the sittings of both the Houses. The move follows a government’s proposal to convene a special sitting of both Houses. As per the Lok Sabha Bulletin, Speaker Om Birla has directed that the Lok Sabha, which was adjourned sine die on the 13th of August, 2026, will now sit at 11 AM on Monday. The Rajya Sabha Bulletin also stated that the Upper House, which was adjourned sine die on the 13th of August, has been reconvened by the Rajya Sabha Chairman, C. P. Radhakrishnan, to meet at 11 AM on Wednesday to transact essential government business. Earlier, the Government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the sittings of the lower house and Upper House on these dates to transact essential Government Business. The Monsoon Session has not been prorogued so far following the adjournment of both the Houses sine die on August 13.
